quick.summary: Why a cold favour gets a no, and how to build trust before you need it.
quick.takeaway: Build trust before you need it.

beats.line: I need a favour from another team. Why won’t they help?
Trust is what lets people say yes without checking.
Think of it as a savings account.
Deposits: keeping promises, sharing credit, helping first.
A favour is a withdrawal. An empty account pays nothing.
So I fake being nice before I need something?
Not fake. Just start before you need anything.
So this week I offer to review their launch notes.
A real deposit. Next time, the yes is easier.

quiz.question: You will need help from another team next quarter. What is the best move now?
options: Ask their manager to tell them
quiz.explanation: Helping first builds the trust that makes a later request easy to say yes to.

quiz.question: Trust built through small, kept promises makes later requests easier.
quiz.explanation: People say yes faster to someone who has already shown they keep their word.
